gaps.sentence: She ___ (think) to be the finest violinist of her generation.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive: is thought to be. The thinkers are general, not stated.

gaps.sentence: The winners ___ a trophy at the closing ceremony.
gaps.hint: passive of a verb with two objects
gaps.explanation: Give somebody something → somebody is given something: future passive will be + given.

gaps.sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ (say) to be on the verge of bankruptcy.
gaps.explanation: It is said that... → The company is said to be... Present simple passive: is said.
Past simple passive: was + demolished. The demolition company is not mentioned.

gaps.sentence: The office ___ (repaint) at the moment, so we're working from home.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are being + past participle. 'At the moment' signals it.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of homes ___ (flood) when the river burst its banks.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + flooded. The cause (the river) is in the when-clause.
